title: Turn a Pile of Screenshots Into One Clean PDF
description: Sending 15 separate screenshots looks messy and unprofessional. Here's how to combine them into a single, ordered PDF in the browser.
excerpt: Fifteen screenshots in an email says amateur. One tidy PDF says you have it together. Here's the two-minute fix.
content:
We all capture screenshots — a receipt, a chat thread, a bug, a booking confirmation. The problem comes when you need to send them. Fifteen separate image attachments look chaotic, arrive out of order, and make simple things look like a mess.

**One PDF beats fifteen images**

A single PDF keeps your screenshots in the right order, opens as one clean document, and looks deliberate. Whether it is evidence for a dispute, a set of instructions, or a chat history for your records, one file is easier to send, read, and store.

**The free workflow**

1. **Gather the screenshots** in the order you want them.
2. **Combine them into a PDF** with [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) — upload the images, arrange the order, export one file. No account, no install.
3. **Compress if it is heavy.** A stack of phone screenshots makes a large PDF; shrink it with [FileTools](https://filetools.eu/pdf-compression) so it fits any inbox.

**Why the browser, not an app**

Screenshots often contain private details — messages, account numbers, personal data. A browser tool that processes files locally means those images are not uploaded to a company's servers. For anything sensitive, that is the safer choice.

**A tidy habit**

Making this your default takes two minutes and changes how your emails land. A colleague, a landlord, or support staff opens one clear document instead of scrolling through a dozen attachments — and quietly takes you more seriously.

Stop attaching screenshots one by one. Stack them into a single PDF and send something that looks like you meant it.
